newsitem.title: USA: Justice says continuing probe of ADM officials.
newsitem.headline: Justice says continuing probe of ADM officials.

text.p: The Justice Department is continuing its investigation of two officials of Archer Daniels Midland Co. in connection with allegations of price fixing, a department official said Tuesday.

The department is still gathering evidence in the case involving the two Archer Daniels officials, Vice Chairman Michael Andreas, and Terrance Wilson, a vice president in charge of ADM's corn refining division, said Deputy Assistant Attorney General Gary Spratling.

Spratling spoke at a press conference with Justice Department officials including Attorney General Janet Reno one day after Archer Daniels said it agreed to plead guilty to federal charges related to price fixing in agricultural products markets and pay fines totalling $100 million.

Reno said the settlement should send a message worldwide to corporations that if they engage in collusive behaviour that hurts U.S. consumers, "there will be vigorous investigation and tough, tough penalties.
The fine was the largest criminal antitrust fine ever.
The agreement settled the Justice Department's investigation of price-fixing of the feed additive lysine and citric acid.

Archer Daniels will pay a fine of $70 million in connection with its plea in lysine, a feed additive used in poultry and swine feed, and $30 million in connection with citric acid, an organic acid used in various foods, beverages and other products.

U.S. Attorney James Burns of the northern district of Illinois, said that under the agreement Archer Daniels officials are required to cooperate with the Justice Department in its ongoing investigation.
"You should stay tuned," said Burns. "There will be more to come.
